provisions.title: Title 1: County Council and Elections
provisions.full_text: 1.02.005 Code may be cited as "K.C.C." The code may be cited by the abbreviation "K.C.C." (Ord. 13880 § 2, 2000).

provisions.title: Title 1: County Council and Elections
provisions.full_text: 1.02.010 Ordinance rules. A rule of construction for ordinances shall be that words signifying the singular number may also be applied to the plural of persons and things; words signifying the plural may be applied to the singular; and words referring to a specific gender may be extended to any other gender. (Ord. 18618 § 1, 2017: Ord. 1371 § 1, 1972).

provisions.title: Title 1: County Council and Elections
provisions.full_text: 1.02.020 Words and phrases  construction. All words and phrases in the King County Code must be construed according to the common and approved usage of the language, but technical words and phrases and such other words and phrases as have acquired a peculiar and appropriate meaning in the law must be construed and understood according to the peculiar and appropriate meaning. (Ord. 13880 § 3, 2000).

provisions.title: Title 1: County Council and Elections
provisions.section_name: Serial commas - standard for ordinances and motions - construction of ordinances and motions before April 17, 2023.
provisions.full_text: 1.02.025 Serial commas - standard for ordinances and motions - construction of ordinances and motions before April 17, 2023. Beginning April 17, 2023, use of the serial comma is the standard for King County ordinances and motions. Ordinances adopted and motions passed before April 17, 2023, that include a listing of three or more items are to be construed to include serial commas unless the context dictates otherwise. (Ord. 19585 § 2, 2023).

provisions.title: Title 1: County Council and Elections
provisions.full_text: 1.02.050 Numbering new sections, chapters--corrections. The clerk of the council shall number new chapters or sections added to the code as the result of enacted ordinances in harmony with the King County Code's general numbering. The sections must bear the respective numbers as are assigned by the clerk. This section does not prohibit or prevent the correction by the clerk of the number of a section of the code found clearly to be incorrectly numbered or incorrectly correlated with other sections as to number. (Ord. 13880 § 6, 2000).

provisions.title: Title 1: County Council and Elections
provisions.full_text: 1.02.060 Expansion of numbering system--decimal factor. Under the King County Code's numbering system, the section factor of the section number must be treated as a decimal figure. In codifying, if new sections must be inserted between sections that are already consecutively numbered, the clerk shall create the proper number for the new section by the insertion of an additional digit at the terminal end of the number of the section immediately preceding the location at which the new section is to be inserted. (Ord. 13880 § 7, 2000).
